whatItIs.text: Yogurt strained of most of its whey — thicker, tangier, and lower in sugar than unstrained yogurt; labneh is strained further still, with salt.

historyNote.text: Strained yogurt only became widely known outside immigrant communities in the 1980s, when the Greek company Fage imported it to the UK as 'Total'; a 2013 UK court case restricted 'Greek yoghurt' to yogurt actually made in Greece, while the US has no legal definition at all — thickened yogurts may be sold as 'Greek'.

howToChoose.text: Check the label: real strained yogurt lists milk and cultures and runs high in protein per 100 g; gum-and-starch thickeners signal 'Greek-style' in all but name.

storage.text: Keep sealed in the fridge with a clean spoon.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Whip Greek yogurt with lemon and garlic for the fastest sauce in the fridge, or strain it overnight into labneh.

substitutions.note: closer thickness; or use less in recipes
